sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Interesting! When both squares are in the black region and I press LEFT:
- Left square: (26, 18) → (26, 14) - moved LEFT by 4 (normal)
- Right square: (30, 46) → (30, 50) - moved RIGHT by 4 (opposite!)
So even when both squares are in the same black region, pressing LEFT makes one move LEFT and the other move RIGHT. They move in OPPOSITE directions!
This is a consistent mechanic: when you press a direction, one square moves in that direction and the other moves in the opposite direction.
Wait, but earlier when both squares were in the upper black region and I pressed UP, they SWAPPED positions (one moved UP, the other moved DOWN). Let me check the earlier data:
- Entry 69, UP: (10, 22) -> (6, 38) and (10, 38) -> (6, 22). 
Hmm, that's not just moving in opposite directions. (10, 22) moved to (6, 38) which is UP and RIGHT. And (10, 38) moved to (6, 22) which is UP and LEFT. So they SWAPPED positions.
But now, pressing LEFT: (26, 18) → (26, 14) (LEFT by 4) and (30, 46) → (30, 50) (RIGHT by 4). They moved in opposite horizontal directions but stayed on the same rows.
So the mechanic might be:
- For LEFT/RIGHT: one square moves LEFT, the other moves RIGHT (opposite horizontal directions)
- For UP/DOWN: one square moves UP, the other moves DOWN (opposite vertical directions)
And the "which square moves which way" depends on their relative positions or some other rule.
Actually, looking at the data:
- LEFT pressed: left square (col 18) moved LEFT to col 14, right square (col 46) moved RIGHT to col 50.
So the left square moved in the commanded direction (LEFT), and the right square moved in the opposite direction (RIGHT).
This suggests: the square that is more to the LEFT moves in the commanded direction, and the other moves opposite. Or maybe it's based on which square was originally on the left.
Let me test this by pressing RIGHT to see if the left square moves RIGHT and the right square moves LEFT.
